name: Jonadab and the Rechabites
charge: Obeying the commandment of Jonadab their father for over two hundred years: no wine, no house, no vineyard, no field
summary: The Lord had Jeremiah set wine before a whole clan in a chamber of the temple. They refused it: their father Jonadab had commanded them to drink none, build no house and sow no seed, and they had kept it all their days. The Lord held them up against Judah, who would not obey him though he rose early and spoke, and promised Jonadab a man before him for ever.
offense: The Rechabites refused the wine Jeremiah set before them in a chamber of the Lord's house. Jonadab their father had commanded them not to drink wine, build houses, sow seed, or plant vineyards, but to dwell in tents. They had kept his charge through their generations. Their presence in Jerusalem was explained by their flight from the invading armies, not by a claim that their ancestral way had been abandoned. Their refusal supplied the contrast God intended. The descendants of Jonadab observed their father's command, while Judah would not hear the Lord despite His repeated sending of prophets. The lesson did not make wine forbidden to everyone; it exposed Judah's refusal to obey the God who had spoken to them.
judgment: Jeremiah announced that Jonadab the son of Rechab would not lack a man to stand before the Lord for ever, because his children had kept his commandment and done all he had charged them. At the same time, God declared the announced evil upon Judah and Jerusalem because He had spoken and they had not heard. The faithful household and the disobedient nation stood side by side, making clear that repeated access to God's word was no substitute for doing it.

entries.commentary: In the days of Jehoiakim the Most High sent Jeremiah to the house of the Rechabites to bring them into the temple chambers and set wine before them to drink. Jaazaniah and the whole house of the Rechabites refused, saying Jonadab the son of Rechab their father commanded them to drink no wine, build no house, sow no seed, and plant no vineyard, but dwell in tents all their days that they might live long in the land. They had obeyed the voice of Jonadab in all things, dwelling in tents, and only came to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans and the Syrians.

The Most High tells Jeremiah to point Judah to the Rechabites: the sons of Jonadab kept their father's command to drink no wine to this day, but this people would not hearken to Him though He rose early and spoke. He sent all His servants the prophets calling every man to return from his evil way, amend his doings, and go not after other gods, promising they would dwell in the land, yet they would not incline their ear. Because the Rechabites obeyed the commandment of their father, Jonadab shall not want a man to stand before Him for ever; but because Judah would not hear or answer, He will bring upon them all the evil He pronounced. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel who kept Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to set up a son and fight, but they are exceedingly afraid because two kings could not stand before him. They submit as his servants, and Jehu's second letter commands them to take the heads of Ahab's seventy sons and bring them to Jezreel by the next day. The heads are laid in two heaps at the gate, and Jehu slays all that remained of the house of Ahab, his great men, kinsfolk, and priests, until none remained, according to the word spoken by Elijah.

Jehu meets the brethren of Ahaziah going to salute the king's children and has all forty-two of them slain at the pit of the shearing house, guilty by association with the house of Ahab. He takes up Jehonadab the son of Rechab, whose heart is right with his, into the chariot to see his zeal for the Most High. At Samaria Jehu slays all that remained unto Ahab, destroying him according to the saying of the Most High spoken to Elijah.

Jehu gathers all the worshippers of Baal by pretending he will serve Baal much more than Ahab did, doing it in subtilty to destroy them. He fills the house of Baal, brings out vestments for every worshipper, and makes sure no servant of the Most High is among them, only Baal worshippers, as with the clergy garments and idolatry seen in false worship today. After the sacrifice he sends in the guard to slay them all, breaks down the images and the house of Baal, and makes it a draught house, so Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel. -

Though Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel, he does not depart from the golden calves that Jeroboam set up in Bethel and in Dan; hold Dan in mind for later scriptures. The Most High commends Jehu for executing what is right against the house of Ahab and promises his children to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel. Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin. -

In those days the Most High begins to cut Israel short, and Hazael smites them in all the coasts from Jordan eastward through Gilead and Bashan. The rest of Jehu's acts are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel, and he reigns twenty-eight years in Samaria before Jehoahaz his son reigns in his place. Jehu's life is a warning that the walk is a marathon, not a sprint, and the difference is whether a man gets back up and repents or stays down and departs from the law. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

verses.text: The word which came unto Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,
Go unto the house of the Rechabites, and speak unto them, and bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink.
Then I took Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habaziniah, and his brethren, and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites;

And I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, a man of God, which was by the chamber of the princes, which was above the chamber of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the door:
And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pots full of wine, and cups, and I said unto them, Drink ye wine.
But they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, neither ye, nor your sons for ever:
Neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any: but all your days ye shall dwell in tents; that ye may live many days in the land where ye be strangers.
Thus have we obeyed the voice of Jonadab the son of Rechab our father in all that he hath charged us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, nor our daughters;
Nor to build houses for us to dwell in: neither have we vineyard, nor field, nor seed:
But we have dwelt in tents, and have obeyed, and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.

But it came to pass, when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came up into the land, that we said, Come, and let us go to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians: so we dwell at Jerusalem.
Then came the word of the Lord unto Jeremiah, saying,
Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Go and tell the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Will ye not receive instruction to hearken to my words? saith the Lord.

The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed; for unto this day they drink none, but obey their father’s commandment: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye hearkened not unto me.

I have sent also unto you all my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them, saying, Return ye now every man from his evil way, and amend your doings, and go not after other gods to serve them, and ye shall dwell in the land which I have given to you and to your fathers: but ye have not inclined your ear, nor hearkened unto me.
Because the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have performed the commandment of their father, which he commanded them; but this people hath not hearkened unto me:

Therefore thus saith the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring upon Judah and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evil that I have pronounced against them: because I have spoken unto them, but they have not heard; and I have called unto them, but they have not answered.

And Jeremiah said unto the house of the Rechabites, Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Because ye have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according unto all that he hath commanded you:
Therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever.

And when he was departed thence, he lighted on Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him: and he saluted him, and said to him, Is thine heart right, as my heart is with thy heart? And Jehonadab answered, It is. If it be, give me thine hand. And he gave him his hand; and he took him up to him into the chariot.
And he said, Come with me, and see my zeal for the Lord. So they made him ride in his chariot.
Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.
Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)
That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.
